newsitem.title: IRAN: Fertiliser mountain may shut Iran petrochem plant.
newsitem.headline: Fertiliser mountain may shut Iran petrochem plant.

text.p: An Iranian petrochemical plant may have to shut down after an apparent dispute with a distribution firm left its storage spaces bulging with 50,000 tonnes of fertiliser, a senior official said in remarks published on Tuesday.

Mojtaba Khosrowtaj, head of the state Petrochemical Commercial Company, said the newly built plant in northeastern Khorasan province might have to cease production unless the firm affiliated with the Agricultural Ministry carried away the urea fertiliser filling its storage, the daily Resalat reported.
Khosrowtaj gave no further details of the apparent dispute.
Iranian media often report about differences between state-run firms required by the government to become more self-reliant as part of Iran's economic liberalisation reforms.
The petrochemical plant, commissioned in July, has an annual capacity to produce 500,000 tonnes of urea fertiliser and 330,000 tonnes of ammonia.
Iran is the Middle East's second largest petrochemical producer behind Saudi Arabia.
